transcript: I just experienced one of the most quietly devastating theater pieces I've seen in a while. It's a new play called “well, I'll let you go” by Bubba Weiler, running at the Irondale in Brooklyn. It's the kind of show that's a little vague and aesthetically minimal in a way that might make you worry it's gonna be nowhere near as profound as it's trying to be, but it ends up actually being really good. It's about the aftermath of someone's death in a nondescript Midwestern town, and it unfolds as a slow burn with impeccable pacing. It's melancholy and ripe with emotional depth brought by an incredible ensemble of actors, led by Quincy Tyler Bernstine. Her performance is a masterclass in restraint and balancing an all-consuming internal churn with an understated sense of realism. I actually felt like the whole production used restraint very effectively, especially in its direction and visual design. In such an intimate space, seemingly small moments hit hard, and you don't need an explosive catharsis to feel right there in these walls of emotion with the characters on stage. I've seen numerous works directed by Jack Serio, and he always makes great use of the spaces he's working in, crafting scenes with just the right amount of energy to fill the room without overflowing it. This one is no different. With that, another program for my collection.
